issue_title: As a merchant I want to know what is tracked during the modules installation step (installer)
issue_body:
As a merchant I want to be informed what data are tracked in the software during modules installation 

## Context

When prestashop is being installed, the project wishes to collect the shop (being installed) URL and the version of PrestaShop being used.
Even if this is compliant with GDPR we wish the user to be fully informed.

## Business rules

During the shop installation (inside installer) - Step 2  (license) 
Add 
- A specific Title (legal information <- Need wording ) 
- A textfied  (need wording)  with 
     - a message / text : it should warn the user that the shop URL will be collected  (need wording) 
     -  add a link to a specific webpage on https://www.prestashop-project.org/ (see https://github.com/PrestaShop/open-source/issues/166)

## Wording

Provided directly in PR by @l-delin : https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/31697#issuecomment-1466090061

issue_title: Issues when upgrading a module used as external source
issue_body:
### Prerequisites - [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug. ### Describe the bug and add attachments When we try to update a module implementing the hook `actionListModules`, if there is any change in the service defintions, the upgrade fails For example, ps_mbo is an external source module, it registers `actionListModules`. That hook returns the fresh data about modules from external APIs During the upgrade process, we are call ```$this->moduleRepository->getModule($name);``` This call will request external sources to get fresh data. In the case it's the module MBO itself which is updating, any changes on service definitions of the new version will lead to a failure Another issue during module upgrade happens when the module listens to event `ModuleManagementEvent::UPGRADE`. The listeners and subcribers are stored on Sf Container build as Closure (see RegisterListenerPass) and until the process ends. So whatever is done in the upgrade process (cache clean, ...) the subscriber will remain the same. If we use some module services in that subscriber and they have changed, ClassLoader will yell because service definitons changed.
To help module developpers to avoid this case, we add a "JS hook" to help modules to execute tasks after a module import ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce 1 - Install mbo 4.0.1 2 - Try to upgrade to 4.3.0 using the button "Install a module" 3 - You'll have an error saying that service `AddonsUser` changed defintion OR 1 - Install v1.0.0 of the example module using the button "Install a module" [prestashopexamplemodule_1.0.0.zip](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/10814931/prestashopexamplemodule_1.0.0.zip) 2 - Install v1.0.1 of the example module using the button "Install a module" [prestashopexamplemodule_1.0.1.zip](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/10814943/prestashopexamplemodule_1.0.1.zip) => this will perform an upgrade ==> You'll have an erreur about array_merge with a value that is not an array ### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened 8.0.x ### PHP version(s) where the bug happened _No response_ ### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version _No response_

issue_title: Upgrading Cancel previous steps in the CI
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing features request](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AImprovement%2CFeature%2CDeveloper+Feature+) and found no previous suggestion of this feature.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

When we push a new commit the CI is launched and the old jobs are not canceled. There already was an attempting to solve this problem but which doesn't work because there is not enough workers.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Every jobs which is not from the last commit push should be canceled automatically.

### Alternatives you've considered

1) We should upgrade every:
```yaml
- name: Cancel Previous Runs
        uses: styfle/cancel-workflow-action@0.9.0
        with:
          access_token: ${{ github.token }}
```
to
```yaml
- name: Cancel Previous Runs
        uses: styfle/cancel-workflow-action@0.9.0
        with:
          all_but_latest: true
          access_token: ${{ github.token }}
```


2) We should add this config on every job which is not based on cron

### Additional context

_No response_

### Do you plan to work on this feature?

- [ ] I'm willing to contribute a [formal specification](https://github.com/PrestaShop/prestashop-specs).
- [ ] I'm willing to provide any wireframes or design assets required for this feature.
- [X] I'm willing to submit a Pull Request that implements this feature.
- [ ] I'm willing to help verify that the implemented feature works as intended and produces no unintended side effects.

issue_title: Cache is cleared for every module when you bulk remove modules instead of only once
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] #29179

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

In the module manager, when you remove multiple modules through bulk action, the cache is cleared for each modules instead of being clearing only once at the end of the process.

### Expected behavior

The cache should be cleared only once at the end of the process.

### Steps to reproduce

As this bug is technical, I think only a dev can validate it:

1. Set a break point to [the clear cache method](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/4a34c76eb9413ac760f37c75ba0dbe6213fd9824/src/Core/Module/EventSubscriber.php#L79)
2. Go to module manager
3. Select multiple modules
4. Click on the bulk action "uninstall"
5. See that the breakpoint is called multiple times

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0.x
